earlier_scan.source_named: Cabico, Jose & de Carvao Chagala, Antonio 2003. Uma breve gramatica da lingua Takwane (SIL Mozambique); also Cabico et al. 2006 notas gramaticais Etakwane. sil.org 403.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives, resources for Takwane [tke] (12 items), page as archived 2016-08-25
sources.note: Bibliographic list only: 2 grammatical descriptions (2003, 2006), 2 thematic dictionaries, 3 survey reports, primers and readers; 'Available Online (4)' are readers/primers, the grammars are 'Not Online'.

sources.citation: Guérois, Rozenn. 2015. A grammar of Cuwabo (Mozambique, Bantu P34). PhD thesis, Université Lumière Lyon 2. hdl:1854/LU-8561497
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: NOT a Takwane source: describes Cuwabo (sister language in Glottolog's Chuwaboic group). Full text searched: 'Takwane'/'Etakwane' does not occur anywhere in the thesis (section 1.3.1 lists only Ethnologue's Cuwabo dialects). Its tone/penultimate-lengthening statements cannot be transferred to Takwane.

sources.citation: Cabiço, José, Jinean Whitley, Oliver Kröger, Manuel Nihoro, Jeffery Shrum & Margaret Shrum. 2006. Algumas notas gramaticais sobre a língua Etakwane. Notas monográficas linguísticas 2. Nampula: Sociedade Internacional de Linguística. 46 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Most recent and longest grammatical description of Takwane (46 pp., co-authored by SIL linguist Oliver Kröger); SIL 'notas gramaticais' booklets normally open with a phonology/orthography section where tone and penultimate lengthening/stress would be stated. Only candidate for a first-hand statement.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Chuwabu language'; Wikipedia (en/pt) Takwane pages; ASJP wordlist TAKWANE; eBible Takwane NT 2009 (Wycliffe)
sources.note: Nothing: no English/Portuguese Wikipedia article on Takwane exists (en redirects to Makhuwa), Chuwabu article does not mention Takwane; ASJP has a wordlist only; eBible is scripture only.

sources.citation: Reiman, Duane. 2002. Findings from the sociolinguistic survey of the Lolo people. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-001. 44 pp.
sources.note: Nothing: sociolinguistic survey (RTT intelligibility of Chuwabu and Takwane by Lolo speakers, lexical similarity percentages, Takwane RTT score tables). a full-text search for stress/accent: no occurrence of stress, tone, accent or penult.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page takw1238 and reference pages 108912 / 49196
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; confirms only two descriptive refs (the two SIL grammar sketches), classification Chuwaboic, alternate name Thakwani, and the SIL ids 47803/45207 (which no longer resolve on sil.org; the live entry numbers are 36558/36507).

sources.citation: Shrum, Jeffery (compiler). 2017-. Takwane Dictionary = Dicionário Takwane. Community reviewed draft. SIL International, published online at Webonary.org (https://www.webonary.org/takwane/), 19 April 2017; last updated 16 September 2024 (3,246 Takwane / 2,626 Portuguese index entries; the SIL Language & Culture Archives record 85153 gives 3,025 entries). Trilingual Takwane-Portuguese-English, extracted from a CAWL-based database.
sources.venue: Trilingual Takwane-Portuguese-English, extracted from a CAWL-based database

tone.summary: Trilingual online dictionary: entries give IPA with vowel length and a few stress marks but no tone marks; its phonology page is an unfilled template. Says nothing about tone.

tone.quote: A ortografia usada neste dicionário segue as recomendações de NELIMO, o Centro de Estudos de Línguas Moçambicanas. Estamos abertos para receber quaisquer sugestões que eventualmente surgirem pela parte dos prezados leitores.
tone.locator: unnumbered preface page, after the contents page and before the first list 'Mmudhi / Família / Family'
tone.translation: The orthography used in this dictionary follows the recommendations of NELIMO, the Centre for the Study of Mozambican Languages. We are open to receiving any suggestions that may arise from our esteemed readers.

sources.note: Record only (unchanged): 4-page SIL Mozambique orthography introduction; content unseen; whether it mentions tone (tom) or only lists graphemes and the double-vowel length convention is unknown.
